summary.intent: Get started on the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge: analyze Soony's supply-chain data drops, decide a product direction, prepare office-hours/interview questions, and build an agent that polls the portal, analyzes changed files with an LLM, and notifies the team.
summary.outcome: Found that Soony's plan says 'all ok' while the Collector's Edition misses Sunday (overbooked art books, failed statue lot, unrealistic pack speed, etc.), published a findings doc, briefing page and Felix interview doc, and built a Python watcher package (poller, versioned store, extractor, pluggable Claude/OpenAI/llama.cpp agent, notifiers) with tests passing; only the PROGRESS.md claim was recorded as modified/committed at the end, and the watcher commit status is unconfirmed.

repo: Portal API has only three endpoints (GET /api/v1/files, /files/{path}, /archive.zip); no notifications or webhooks, so changes must be detected by polling the file list and comparing SHA-256 checksums.
Existing portal files can be replaced under the same name, so change detection must compare checksums, not just filenames; formats (columns, delimiters, encodings) may also change.
Confidential portal data lives in the gitignored data/ folder; .env is gitignored and .env.example is committed with SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN empty.
Teammates added CLAUDE.md and PROGRESS.md as a team workflow; tasks are claimed via a 'Now' line in PROGRESS.md.
Repo is a Python package under src/ask_soony (config, portal, store, extract, llm backends, agent, notify, watcher, cli) with tests using invented data and fake portal/LLM responses.
Large first syncs should use archive.zip rather than per-file downloads; portal client needed retries.
Entire hooks skip creating a checkpoint when no repo files were modified during the session; checkpoints appear at the first commit with session changes.
workflow: Subagents are effective for bulk cross-checking (200 order confirmations vs SAP, 59 scans) and surfaced the key discrepancies.
Scanned PDFs need to be rendered to images to be read; the extractor handles scans as images and text files as text.
Commit author must be set via env vars to use the user's author address without a session trailer.
Keep confidential data and the user's login details out of docs and commits; the portal password shared in chat should be rotated after the hack.
Claude Docs artifacts need a check for others' edits before rewriting a section.

friction: Portal token was initially empty in .env, causing 401s and blocking data access until supplied.
The first baseline poll failed and needed fixes (imports, archive-based sync, retries) before succeeding.
The computer went to sleep mid-response, interrupting the README/.env.example documentation step.
Initial commit attempt used the wrong author and had to be redone with env vars.
Unclear whether portal data and supplier replies differ per team; unresolved without asking the Lio engineers.
Page published without a rendered preview, so its appearance is unverified.
